name: somagic
desc: Linux capture program for the Somagic variants of EasyCAP
why: A Linux capture driver for old EasyCAP video dongles, a rewarding hardware rabbit hole despite its archived state.

brief.what_it_is: somagic is a Linux capture program for the Somagic variants of EasyCAP, the cheap USB video-capture dongles that take analogue composite or S-Video in. The package ships two executables, somagic-capture and somagic-init. From the Homebrew description alone, the input is the dongle's video and the capture tool records it on Linux; I could not confirm the output format or any options. The homepage did not render any project content, so this description comes from the Homebrew metadata.
brief.why_it_exists: It exists to make the Somagic-chipset EasyCAP devices usable on Linux. The homepage gave no author framing that I could read, because the page only showed a JavaScript notice.

commands_seen.context: Named in the Homebrew caveat as the capture program that must not be run until the official firmware has been extracted from the CD. I did not see its arguments or usage.

brief.install_notes: Homebrew caveat: before running somagic-capture you must extract the official firmware from the CD. The caveat points to a GettingStarted.wiki page on the old Google Code site, which I could not read. Expect a physical EasyCAP dongle and the vendor's install CD for firmware. I found no other runtime or account requirements.
brief.standout: The firmware has to be pulled from the vendor's own CD before the driver will work, so the install step is a hardware-and-media chore rather than a download. It is a small, single-purpose driver for a specific cheap device, which makes it a satisfying hardware rabbit hole.
brief.status: Quiet/archived. The homepage is a Google Code Archive page, and Google Code has been shut down, so the project is read-only there. I saw no release date or last-commit date, so I cannot say more than that.
brief.caveats: The homepage and the GettingStarted wiki both returned only a 'requires JavaScript' shell, so I read no README, usage docs, or source. Everything beyond the Homebrew description is unverified. The firmware must come from the official CD, which is a barrier. The project is archived. I found no licence information.
quotes: Before running somagic-capture you must extract the official firmware from the CD.
